metadata.title: A formalised proof of Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent 3 in the Lean proof assistant.

nodes.statement: Let $p \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ be prime. \\\\ If $\zeta_p$ is a primitive $p$-th root of unity, then $\zeta_p - 1$ is prime.
nodes.label: thm:zeta_sub_one_prime1

Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, domain and normalised $\gcd$ monoid.\\ Let $a, b, c \in R$. \\ Let $n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$. \\\\ Then, to prove Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent $n$ in $R$, one can assume, without loss of generality, that $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$.

Let $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_9$ be the ring of integers modulo $9$. \\ Let $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_3$ be the ring of integers modulo $3$. \\ Let $n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_9$. \\ Let $\phi : \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_9 \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_3$ be the canonical ring homomorphism. \\ Let $\phi(n) \neq 0$. \\ \\ Then $n^3=1 \lor n^3=8$.
nodes.label: lmm:cube_of_castHom_ne_zero

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $u \in \mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be a unit. \\\\ Then $u \in \ensuremath{\left\{1, -1, \eta, -\eta, \eta^2, -\eta^2\right\}}$.
nodes.label: thm:mem

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the fundamental system of $K$. \\ By properties of cyclotomic fields, we know that $\mathrm{rank}\left(K\right) = 0$ (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Embeddings.html#NumberField.InfinitePlace.card_eq_nrRealPlaces_add_nrComplexPlaces}{this lemma}, \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/FLT3/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Embeddings.html#IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.nrRealPlaces_eq_zero}{this lemma} and \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/FLT3/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Embeddings.html#IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.nrComplexPlaces_eq_totient_div_two}{this lemma} which have already been formalised and included in Mathlib). By the Dirichlet Unit Theorem (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units.html#NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod}{Mathlib}), we know that $$\exists x \in K \text{ with finite order, such that } u = x \prod_{v\in\mathcal{F}} v,$$ but since $\mathrm{rank}\left(K\right) = 0$, then $\mathcal{F} = \emptyset$, which implies that $u = x$.\\ Since $u = x$ has finite order, by properties of primitive roots (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/PrimitiveRoots.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.exists_pow_or_neg_mul_pow_of_isOfFinOrder}{this lemma} that has already been formalised and included in Mathlib), we can deduce that $$\exists r < 3 \text{ such that } u = \eta^r \lor u = -\eta^r.$$ Therefore, we can conclude $$u \in \ensuremath{\left\{\pm \eta^r\mid r \in \ensuremath{\left\{0,1,2\right\}}\right\}} = \ensuremath{\left\{1, -1, \eta, -\eta, \eta^2, -\eta^2\right\}}.$$

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$. \\\\ Then $3 \nmid \eta - m$.
nodes.label: thm:not_exists_int_three_dvd_sub

nodes.statement: By properties of cyclotomic fields, we know that $\ensuremath{\left\{1,\eta\right\}}$ is an integral power basis of $\mathcal{O}_K$ (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/FLT3/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Rat.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.integralPowerBasis'}{this lemma}, \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/FLT3/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Rat.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.power_basis_int'_dim}{this lemma} and \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/FLT3/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Rat.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.integralPowerBasis'_gen}{this lemma} which have already been formalised and included in Mathlib).\\ For every $\xi \in \mathcal{O}_K$, we define $\pi_1(\xi)$ and $\pi_2(\xi)$ to be the first and second coordinates of $\xi$ with respect to the basis $\ensuremath{\left\{1,\eta\right\}} \in \mathcal{O}_K$, i.e. $$\xi = \pi_1(\xi) + \pi_2(\xi)\eta.$$ By contradiction we assume that $$\exists m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \text{ such that } 3 \mid \eta - m,$$ which implies that $$\exists x \in \mathcal{O}_K \text{ such that } \eta - m = 3 x.$$ By linearity of $\pi_2$, $$\pi_2(\eta) = \pi_2(3x + m) = 3\pi_2(x) + \pi_2(m).$$ Since $\pi_2(\eta) = 1$ and $\pi_2(m) = 0$, then we have that $3 \mid 1$, which is a contradiction.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda^2 = -3 \eta$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_sq

nodes.statement: By definition we have that $\lambda = \eta -1$, which implies that $$\lambda^2 = (\eta - 1)^2 = \eta^2 - 2\eta + 1.$$ Since $\eta$ corresponds to a root of the equation $x^2 + x + 1 = 0$, then $\eta^2 = -1 - \eta$. Substituting back, we can conclude that $$\lambda^2 = (-1 - \eta) - 2\eta + 1 = -3\eta.$$

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $u \in \mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be a unit. \\\\ If $\exists m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ such that $\lambda^2 \mid u - m$, then $u = 1 \lor u = -1$. \\ This is a special case of the Kummer's Lemma.
nodes.label: lmm:eq_one_or_neg_one_of_unit_of_congruent

nodes.statement:
By \Cref{lmm:lambda_sq}, we have that $-3\eta = \lambda^2 \mid u - m$, which implies that $3 \mid u - m$.\ By \Cref{thm:mem}, we know that $u \in \ensuremath{\left\{1, -1, \eta, -\eta, \eta^2, -\eta^2ight\}}$. \ We proceed by analysing each case:  egin{itemize} \item Case $u = 1 \lor u = -1$. This finishes the proof. \item Case $u = \eta$.\ Since $3 \mid u - m$, we have that $3 \mid \eta - m$, which contradicts \Cref{thm:not_exists_int_three_dvd_sub} forcing us to conclude that $u 
eq \eta$. \item Case $u = -\eta$.\ Since $3 \mid u - m$, we have that $3 \mid - \eta - m$, then by properties of divisibility $3 \mid \eta + m$, which contradicts \Cref{thm:not_exists_int_three_dvd_sub} forcing us to conclude that $u 
eq -\eta$. \item Case $u = \eta^2$.\ Since $3 \mid u - m$, we have that $3 \mid \eta^2 - m$, which contradicts \Cref{thm:not_exists_int_three_dvd_sub} since $\eta^2$ is a third root of unity (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Basic.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.pow_of_coprime}{Mathlib}), forcing us to conclude that $u 
eq \eta^2$. \item Case $u = -\eta^2$.\ Since $3 \mid u - m$, we have that $3 \mid - \eta^2 - m$, then by properties of divisibility $3 \mid \eta^2 + m$, which contradicts \Cref{thm:not_exists_int_three_dvd_sub} since $\eta^2$ is a third root of unity (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Basic.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.pow_of_coprime}{Mathlib}), forcing us to conclude that $u 
eq -\eta^2$. \end{itemize} Therefore, $u = 1 \lor u = -1$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then the norm of $\lambda$ is $3$.
nodes.label: lmm:norm_lambda

nodes.statement: Since the third cyclotomic polynomial over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$ is irreducible, then the norm of $\lambda$ is $3$ by properties of primitive roots (see \href{https://pitmonticone.github.io/FLT3/docs/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/PrimitiveRoots.html#IsPrimitiveRoot.sub_one_norm_prime}{this lemma} that has already been formalised and included in Mathlib).

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then the norm of $\lambda$ is a prime number.
nodes.label: lmm:norm_lambda_prime

nodes.statement: It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:norm_lambda} since $3$ is a prime number.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \mid 3$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_dvd_three

nodes.statement: By properties of norms and divisibility, if the norm of an element in the ring of integers divides a number, then the element itself must divide that number. In this case, by \Cref{lmm:norm_lambda} we know that the norm of $\lambda$ is $3$, that divides $3$, which implies that $\lambda \mid 3$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda$ is prime.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_prime

nodes.statement: Since $3$ is prime and $\zeta_3$ is a primitive third root of unity, then $\lambda$ is prime by \Cref{thm:zeta_sub_one_prime1}.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \neq 0$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_ne_zero

nodes.statement: It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:lambda_prime} since zero is not prime.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda$ is not a unit.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_not_unit

nodes.statement: It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:lambda_prime} since prime numbers are not units.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. \\\\ Then $\mathcal{O}_K / I$ has cardinality $3$.
nodes.label: lmm:card_quot

nodes.statement: It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:norm_lambda} by the fundamental properties of ideals.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. \\ Let $2 \in \mathcal{O}_K / I$. \\\\ Then $2 \neq 0$.
nodes.label: lmm:two_ne_zero

nodes.statement:
By contradiction we assume that $2 \in I$, then, by definition, $\lambda$ would divide $2 \in \mathcal{O}_K$. Recall from \Cref{lmm:norm_lambda} that the norm of $\lambda$ is $3$. If $\lambda$ divided $2$, then by properties of divisibility in number fields, the norm of $\lambda$ would also divide $2$. However $3 
mid 2$ showing a contradiction. Therefore, $\lambda 
mid 2$, then $2 
otin I$, which implies that $2 \in \mathcal{O}_K / I$ is non-zero.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \nmid 2$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_not_dvd_two

nodes.statement: By contradiction we assume that $\lambda \mid 2$, that implies that $2 \in I$ from which it follows that $2 = 0$ contradicting \Cref{lmm:two_ne_zero} forcing us to conclude that $\lambda \nmid 2$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. \\\\ Then $\mathcal{O}_K / I = \ensuremath{\left\{0, 1, -1\right\}}$.
nodes.label: lmm:univ_quot

nodes.statement: By \Cref{lmm:card_quot}, the cardinality of $\mathcal{O}_K / I$ is $3$, so it suffices to prove that $1,-1$ and $0$ are distinct.\\ We proceed by contradiction analysing each case: \begin{itemize} \item Case $1 = -1$. By basic algebraic properties, $1 = -1$ implies that $2 = 0$, which contradicts \Cref{lmm:two_ne_zero} forcing us to conclude that $1 \neq -1$. \item Case $1 = 0$. Trivial contradiction. \item Case $-1 = 0$. It implies that $1 = 0$, which is a contradiction. \end{itemize}

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$. \\\\ Then $(\lambda \mid x) \lor (\lambda \mid x-1) \lor (\lambda \mid x+1)$.
nodes.label: lmm:dvd_or_dvd_sub_one_or_dvd_add_one

nodes.statement: Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. Let $\pi : \mathcal{O}_K \to \mathcal{O}_K / I$.\\ By \Cref{lmm:univ_quot}, we have that $\pi(x) \in \mathcal{O}_K / I = \ensuremath{\left\{0, 1, -1\right\}}$.\\ We proceed by analysing each case: \begin{itemize} \item Case $\pi(x) = 0$. By properties of ideals, $\lambda \mid x$. \item Case $\pi(x) = 1$. Then $0=\pi(x)-1=\pi(x-1)$, which, by properties of ideals, implies that $\lambda \mid x-1$. \item Case $\pi(x) = -1$. Then $0=\pi(x)+1=\pi(x+1)$, which, by properties of ideals, implies that $\lambda \mid x+1$. \end{itemize}

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\\\ Then $\eta^3 = 1$.
nodes.label: lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one

nodes.statement: Since $\zeta_3 \in K$ is a primitive third root of unity, then $\zeta_3^3 = 1$. Given that $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ is the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$, then $\eta^3 = 1$ by the extension of the field properties into the ring of integers.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\\\ Then $\eta$ is a unit.
nodes.label: lmm:eta_isUnit

nodes.statement: It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one}.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\\\ Then $\eta^2 + \eta + 1 = 0$.
nodes.label: lmm:toInteger_eval_cyclo

nodes.statement: Since $\eta$ corresponds to a root of the equation $x^2 + x + 1 = 0$, then $\eta^2 + \eta + 1 = 0$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$. \\\\ Then $x^3 - 1 = (x - 1)(x - \eta)(x - \eta^ 2)$.
nodes.label: lmm:cube_sub_one

nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one} and \Cref{lmm:toInteger_eval_cyclo}, we have that \begin{align*} (x - 1)(x - \eta)(x - \eta^ 2) &= x^3 - x^2 (\eta^2 + \eta + 1) + x (\eta^2 + \eta + \eta^3) - \eta^3 \\ &= x^3 - x^2 (\eta^2 + \eta + 1) + x (\eta^2 + \eta + 1) - 1 \\ &= x^3 - 1. \end{align*}

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \mid x(x - 1)(x - (\eta + 1))$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_dvd_mul_sub_one_mul_sub_eta_add_one

nodes.statement: By \Cref{lmm:dvd_or_dvd_sub_one_or_dvd_add_one}, we have that $$(\lambda \mid x) \lor (\lambda \mid x-1) \lor (\lambda \mid x+1).$$ We proceed by analysing each case: \begin{itemize} \item Case $\lambda \mid x$. \\ By properties of divisibility, we have that $\lambda \mid x(x - 1)(x - (\eta + 1))$. \item Case $\lambda \mid x-1$. \\ By properties of divisibility, we have that $\lambda \mid x(x - 1)(x - (\eta + 1))$. \item Case $\lambda \mid x+1$.\\ By properties of divisibility, it suffices to prove that $$\lambda \mid x - (\eta + 1) = x + 1 - (\eta - 1 + 3).$$ By definition of $\lambda$, we have that $$x + 1 - (\eta - 1 + 3) = x + 1 - (\lambda + 3).$$ By properties of divisibility and \Cref{lmm:lambda_dvd_three}, we can deduce that $\lambda \mid \lambda + 3$.\\ Therefore, by properties of divisibility, we can conclude that $$\lambda \mid x(x - 1)(x - (\eta + 1)).$$ \end{itemize}

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$. \\\\ If $\lambda\mid x - 1$, then $\lambda^ 4 \mid x^3 - 1$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_pow_four_dvd_cube_sub_one_of_dvd_sub_one

nodes.statement: Let $\lambda \mid x - 1$, which is equivalent to say that $$\exists y\in \mathcal{O}_K \text{ such that } x - 1 = \lambda y.$$ By ring properties and \Cref{lmm:cube_sub_one}, we have that $$x^3 - 1 = \lambda^3 (y (y - 1) (y - (\eta + 1))).$$ By properties of divisibility and \Cref{lmm:lambda_dvd_mul_sub_one_mul_sub_eta_add_one}, we can conclude that $$\lambda^ 4 \mid x^3 - 1.$$

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$. \\\\ If $\lambda \mid x + 1$, then $\lambda^4 \mid x ^ 3 + 1$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_pow_four_dvd_cube_add_one_of_dvd_add_one

nodes.statement: By properties of divisibility, if $\lambda \mid x + 1$ then $$\lambda \mid - (x + 1) = (- x) - 1.$$ By \Cref{lmm:lambda_dvd_mul_sub_one_mul_sub_eta_add_one}, we can deduce that $$\lambda^ 4 \mid (-x)^3 - 1.$$ By divisibility and ring properties we can conclude that $$\lambda^ 4 \mid x^3 + 1.$$

By contradiction we assume that $$(\lambda^2 
mid a + b) \land (\lambda^2 
mid a + \eta b) \land (\lambda^2 
mid a + \eta^2 b).$$ Then, by definition, the multiplicity of $\lambda$ in $a + b$, in $a + \eta b$ and in $a + \eta^2 b$ is less than $2$. By properties of divisibility, \Cref{lmm:lambda_pow_two_dvd_c} and \Cref{lmm:cube_add_cube_eq_mul}, we have that $$\lambda^6 \mid u c^3 = a^3 + b^3 = (a + b) (a + \eta b) (a + \eta^2 b).$$ Then, the multiplicity of $\lambda$ in $(a + b) (a + \eta b) (a + \eta^2 b)$ is greater than or equal to $6$. \ By \Cref{lmm:lambda_prime} $\lambda$ is prime, so we have that the multiplicity of $\lambda$ in $(a + b) (a + \eta b) (a + \eta^2 b)$ is the sum of the multiplicities of $\lambda$ in $a + b$, in $a + \eta b$ and in $a + \eta^2 b$, which is less than $6$. This is a contradiction that forces us to conclude that $$(\lambda^2 \mid a + b) \lor (\lambda^2 \mid a + \eta b) \lor (\lambda^2 \mid a + \eta^2 b).$$

Trivial using $a_1=a$ and $b_1=b$. \item Case $\lambda^2 \mid a + \eta b$. Let $a_1=a$ and $b_1=\eta b$. \ By \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one}, we have that $a^3 + (\eta b)^3 = a^3 + b^3 = u c^3$.\ By properties of coprimes and \Cref{lmm:eta_isUnit}, we have that $\gcd(a,b)=1$ implies that $\gcd(a,\eta b)=1$.\ Since $a_1=a$, we already know that $\lambda 
mid a = a_1$.\ By contradiction we assume that $\lambda \mid b_1 = \eta b$, which, by \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one}, it implies that $\lambda \mid \eta^2 \eta b = b$ that contradicts our assumption, forcing us to conclude that $\lambda 
mid b_1$. \item Case $\lambda^2 \mid a + \eta^2 b$. Let $a_1=a$ and $b_1=\eta^2 b$. \ By \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one}, we have that $a^3 + (\eta^2 b)^3 = a^3 + b^3 = u c^3$.\ By properties of coprimes and \Cref{lmm:eta_isUnit}, we have that $\gcd(a,b)=1$ implies that $\gcd(a,\eta^2 b)=1$.\ Since $a_1=a$, we already know that $\lambda 
mid a = a_1$.\ By contradiction we assume that $\lambda \mid b_1 = \eta^2 b$, which, by \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one}, it implies that $\lambda \mid \eta \eta^2 b = b$ that contradicts our assumption, forcing us to conclude that $\lambda 
mid b_1$. \end{itemize} Therefore, we can conclude that $\exists a_1,b_1 \in \mathcal{O}_k$ such that $S_1=(a_1,b_1,c,u)$ is a $solution$.

It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:lambda_prime}. \item Case $p \nmid \lambda$. \\ By hypothesis, we have that $p \mid a+ b$ and $p \mid a+\eta^2 b$. By \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one} and \Cref{lmm:eta_isUnit}, we have that $$p \mid \eta ((a+\eta^2 b) - (a+ b)) = - (\eta^3 - \eta) b = \lambda b,$$ which implies that $p \mid b$ and we proceed analogously to show that $p \mid a$.\\ Therefore $p \mid \gcd(a,b)=1$ which is absurd. \end{itemize} Therefore, we can conclude that $p$ is associated with $\lambda$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S=(a, b, c, u)$ be a $solution$.\\ Let $p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be a prime such that $p \mid a+\eta b$ and $p \mid a+\eta^2 b$.\\\\ Then $p$ is associated with $\lambda$.
nodes.label: lmm:associated_of_dvd_a_add_eta_mul_b_of_dvd_a_add_eta_sq_mul_b

nodes.statement: We proceed by analysis each case: \begin{itemize} \item Case $p \mid \lambda$. It directly follows from \Cref{lmm:lambda_prime}. \item Case $p \nmid \lambda$. \\ By hypothesis, we have that $p \mid a+\eta b$ and $p \mid a+\eta^2 b$. Then $p \mid (a+\eta^2 b) - (a+\eta b) = \eta b (\eta-1) = \eta b \lambda$, which, by \Cref{lmm:eta_isUnit}, implies that $p \mid b$ and we proceed analogously to show that $p \mid a$.\\ Therefore $p \mid \gcd(a,b)=1$ which is absurd. \end{itemize} Therefore, we can conclude that $p$ is associated with $\lambda$.

nodes.statement: By \Cref{def:Solution_Multiplicity} we have that $\lambda^n \mid c$. Since $u$ is a unit, then by \Cref{lmm:cube_add_cube_eq_mul} we have that $$\lambda^{3n} \mid u c^3 = a^3 + b^3 = (a+b)(a + \eta b)(a + \eta^2 b) = (a+b)(\lambda y)(\lambda z).$$ Then applying \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_y} and \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_z}, we can conclude that $\lambda^{3n-2} \mid a+b$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\lambda \nmid w$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\lambda \nmid x$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_not_dvd_x

nodes.statement: By contradiction, if $\lambda \mid x$, then $\lambda^{3n-1} \mid \lambda^{3n-2} x = a+b$. Using \Cref{lmm:lambda_dvd_a_add_eta_mul_b} and \Cref{lmm:lambda_dvd_a_add_eta_sq_mul_b}, we have that $\lambda^{3n+1} \mid (a+b) (a + \eta b) (a + \eta^2 cdot b) = a^3+b^3 = u c^3 = u \lambda^{3n} w^3$. Then $\lambda \mid w^3$ which implies that $\lambda \mid w$, that contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_w} forcing us to conclude $\lambda \nmid x$.
Let $S$ be a $solution$ with multiplicity $n$.\\\\ Then $\gcd(x,y) = 1$.
nodes.label: lmm:coprime_x_y

nodes.statement:
Since $y 
eq 0$ by \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_y}, by the properties of PIDs it suffices to prove that $ orall p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ if $p$ is prime and $p \mid x$, then $p 
mid y$. Let $p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be prime and suppose by contradiction that $p \mid x$ and $p \mid y$ which implies that $p \mid \lambda^{3n-2} x = a+b$ and $p \mid \lambda y = a + \eta b$. Then by \Cref{lmm:associated_of_dvd_a_add_b_of_dvd_a_add_eta_mul_b} we have that $p$ is associated with $\lambda$, which implies that $\lambda \mid x$ that contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_x} forcing us to conclude that $p 
mid y$, which, as stated above, implies that $\gcd(x,y)=1$.
Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\gcd(x,z) = 1$.
nodes.label: lmm:coprime_x_z

nodes.statement:
Since $z 
eq 0$ by \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_z}, by the properties of PIDs it suffices to prove that $ orall p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ if $p$ is prime and $p \mid x$, then $p 
mid z$. Let $p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be prime and suppose by contradiction that $p \mid x$ and $p \mid z$ which implies that $p \mid \lambda^{3n-2} x = a+b$ and $p \mid \lambda z = a + \eta^2 b$. Then by \Cref{lmm:associated_of_dvd_a_add_b_of_dvd_a_add_eta_sq_mul_b} we have that $p$ is associated with $\lambda$, which implies that $\lambda \mid x$ that contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_x} forcing us to conclude that $p

Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\gcd(y, z) = 1$.

Since $z 
eq 0$ by \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_z}, by the properties of PIDs it suffices to prove that $ orall p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ if $p$ is prime and $p \mid y$, then $p 
mid z$. Let $p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be prime and suppose by contradiction that $p \mid y$ and $p \mid z$ which implies that $p \mid \lambda y = a+\eta b$ and $p \mid \lambda z = a + \eta^2 b$. Then by \Cref{lmm:associated_of_dvd_a_add_eta_mul_b_of_dvd_a_add_eta_sq_mul_b} we have that $p$ is associated with $\lambda$, which implies that $\lambda \mid y$ that contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_y} forcing us to conclude that $p

nodes.label: lmm:x_mul_y_mul_z_eq_u_w_pow_three

nodes.statement: By the properties of PIDs, it suffices to prove that there exists a $k\in \mathcal{O}_K$ such that $xk$ is a cube and $\gcd(x,k)=1$. Let $k = yzu^{-1}$, then $xk = x y z u^{-1} = w^3$ by \Cref{lmm:x_mul_y_mul_z_eq_u_w_pow_three}. Moreover, since $\gcd(x,y)=1$ by \Cref{lmm:coprime_x_y} and $\gcd(x,z)=1$ by \Cref{lmm:coprime_x_z}, then $\gcd(x,yz)=1$, which implies that $\gcd(x,k)=1$.
Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\exists u_2 \in \mathcal{O}^\times_K$ and $\exists Y \in \mathcal{O}_K$ such that $y = u_2 Y^3$.
nodes.label: lmm:y_eq_unit_mul_cube

Let $k = xzu^{-1}$, then $yk = y x z u^{-1} = w^3$ by \Cref{lmm:x_mul_y_mul_z_eq_u_w_pow_three}. Moreover, since $\gcd(x,y)=1$ by \Cref{lmm:coprime_x_y} and $\gcd(y,z)=1$ by \Cref{lmm:coprime_y_z}, then $\gcd(y,xz)=1$, which implies that $\gcd(y,k)=1$.

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ We define $u_1 \in \mathcal{O}^\times_K$ and $X \in \mathcal{O}_K$ such that $x = u_1 X^3$.\\ We define $u_2 \in \mathcal{O}^\times_K$ and $Y \in \mathcal{O}_K$ such that $y = u_2 Y^3$.\\ We define $u_3 \in \mathcal{O}^\times_K$ and $Z \in \mathcal{O}_K$ such that $z = u_3 Z^3$.\\ We define $u_4 = \eta u_3 u_2^{-1}$.\\ We define $u_5 = -\eta^2 u_1 u_2^{-1}$.\\
nodes.label: def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $X \neq 0$.
nodes.label: lmm:X_ne_zero

nodes.statement: By contradiction we assume that $X = 0$, then $x = 0$ by \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z}. Therefore $\lambda$ trivially divides $x$ (as any number divides zero) which contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_x} forcing us to conclude that $X \neq 0$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\lambda \nmid X$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_not_dvd_X

nodes.statement: By contradiction we assume that $\lambda \mid X$, then, by the properties of divisibility, $\lambda \mid u_1 X^3$, which implies, by \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z}, that $\lambda \mid x$. However, this contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_x} forcing us to conclude that $\lambda \nmid X$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\lambda \nmid Y$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_not_dvd_Y

nodes.statement: By contradiction we assume that $\lambda \mid Y$, then, by the properties of divisibility, $\lambda \mid u_2 Y^3$, which implies, by \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z}, that $\lambda \mid y$. However, this contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_y} forcing us to conclude that $\lambda \nmid Y$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\lambda \nmid Z$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_not_dvd_Z

nodes.statement: By contradiction we assume that $\lambda \mid Z$, then, by the properties of divisibility, $\lambda \mid u_3 Z^3$, which implies, by \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z}, that $\lambda \mid z$. However, this contradicts \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_z} forcing us to conclude that $\lambda \nmid Z$.
Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\gcd(Y, Z) = 1$.
nodes.label: lmm:coprime_Y_Z

nodes.statement:
Since $Z 
eq 0$ by \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_Z}, by the properties of PIDs it suffices to prove that $ orall p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ if $p$ is prime and $p \mid Y$, then $p 
mid Z$. Let $p \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be prime and suppose by contradiction that $p \mid Y$ and $p \mid Z$ which implies that $p \mid u_2 Y^3 = y$ and $p \mid \lambda u_3 Z^3 = z$. But this contradicts \Cref{lmm:coprime_y_z} forcing us to conclude that $p 
mid Z$, which, as stated above, implies that $\gcd(Y,Z)=1$.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$ with multiplicity $n$.\\\\ Then $u_1 X^3 \lambda^{3n-2}+u_2 \eta Y^3 \lambda + u_3 \eta^2 Z^3 \lambda = 0$.
nodes.label: lmm:formula1

nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z}, \Cref{def:Solution_x_y_z_w}, \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one} and \Cref{lmm:toInteger_eval_cyclo}, we have \begin{align*} u_1 X^3 \lambda^{3n-2}+u_2 \eta Y^3 \lambda + u_3 \eta^2 Z^3 \lambda &= x \lambda^{3n-2} + \eta y \lambda + \eta^2 z \lambda \\ &= (a+b) + \eta (a+\eta b) + \eta^2 (a+\eta^2 b) \\ &= a (1 + \eta + \eta^2) + b (1 + \eta^4 + \eta^2) \\ &= (a+b)(1+\eta+\eta^2)\\ &= (a+b)0 = 0 \end{align*}
Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $u_4$ is a unit.
nodes.label: lmm:u₄_isUnit

nodes.statement: By \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z} $u_4 = \eta u_3 u_2^{-1}$, which is a product of units by \Cref{lmm:eta_isUnit}. Since the product of units is a unit (multiplicative closure), it follows that $u_4$ must also be a unit.
Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $u_5$ is a unit.
nodes.label: lmm:u₅_isUnit

nodes.statement: By \Cref{def:Solution_u1_u2_u3_u4_u5_X_Y_Z} $u_5 = -\eta^2 u_1 u_2^{-1}$, which is a product of units since $\eta^3 = 1$ by \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one} and $-\eta (-\eta^2) = \eta^3$. Since the product of units is a unit (multiplicative closure), it follows that $u_5$ must also be a unit.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$ with multiplicity $n$.\\\\ Then $Y^3 + u_4 Z^3 = u_5 (\lambda^(n-1) X)^3$.
nodes.label: lmm:formula2

nodes.statement: Using \Cref{lmm:eta_isUnit}, \Cref{lmm:lambda_ne_zero}, it suffices to show that $$\lambda \eta u_2 (Y^3 + u_4 Z^3) = \lambda \eta u_2 u_5 (\lambda^(n-1) X)^3$$ which can be proved by simple calculations involving \Cref{lmm:toInteger_cube_eq_one}, \Cref{lmm:Solution_two_le_multiplicity} and \Cref{lmm:formula1}.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $\lambda^2 \mid \lambda^4$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_sq_div_lambda_fourth

nodes.statement: Straightforward application of the definition of divisibility.

Let $K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}_K = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\mathcal{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\mathcal{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S$ be a $solution$ with multiplicity $n$.\\\\ Then $\lambda^2 \mid u_5 (\lambda^{n - 1} X)^3$.
nodes.label: lmm:lambda_sq_div_new_X_cubed

nodes.statement: Using \Cref{lmm:Solution_two_le_multiplicity}, we have that $\lambda^2 \mid \lambda^2 u_5 \lambda^{3n-5} X^3 = u_5 (\lambda^{n - 1} X)^3$.
Let $S$ be a $solution$.\\\\ Then $u_4 \in \ensuremath{\left\{-1,1\right\}} \subset \mathcal{O}_K$.

nodes.statement: Let $n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ be the multiplicity of the solution $S$.\\ By \Cref{lmm:eq_one_or_neg_one_of_unit_of_congruent}, it suffices to prove that $$\exists m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \text{ such that } \lambda^2 \mid u_4 - m.$$ By \Cref{lmm:lambda_pow_four_dvd_cube_sub_one_or_add_one_of_lambda_not_dvd} and \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_Y}, we have that $$(\lambda^4 \mid Y^3 - 1) \lor (\lambda^4 \mid Y^3 + 1).$$ By \Cref{lmm:lambda_pow_four_dvd_cube_sub_one_or_add_one_of_lambda_not_dvd} and \Cref{lmm:lambda_not_dvd_Z}, we have that $$(\lambda^4 \mid Z^3 - 1) \lor (\lambda^4 \mid Z^3 + 1).$$ We proceed by analysing each case: \begin{itemize} \item Case $(\lambda^4 \mid Y^3 - 1) \land (\lambda^4 \mid Z^3 - 1)$. \\ Let $m=-1$ and consider the fact that $$u_4 - m = Y^3 + u_4 Z^3 - (Y^3 - 1) - u_4 (Z^3 - 1).$$ By \Cref{lmm:formula2}, we have that $$u_4 - m = u_5 (\lambda^{n-1} X)^3 - (Y^3 - 1) - u_4 (Z^3 - 1).$$ Since, by \Cref{lmm:lambda_sq_div_new_X_cubed}, we know that $$\lambda^2 \mid u_5 (\lambda^{n-1} X)^3$$ and, by \Cref{lmm:lambda_sq_div_lambda_fourth} and by assumption, we have that $$\lambda^2 \mid Y^3 - 1 \land \lambda^2 \mid Z^3 - 1,$$ Then, we can conclude that $$\lambda^2 \mid u_4 - m.$$ \item Case $(\lambda^4 \mid Y^3 - 1) \land (\lambda^4 \mid Z^3 + 1)$. \\ Let $m=1$ and proceed similarly to the first case. \item Case $(\lambda^4 \mid Y^3 + 1) \land (\lambda^4 \mid Z^3 - 1)$. \\ Let $m=1$ and proceed similarly to the first case. \item Case $(\lambda^4 \mid Y^3 + 1) \land (\lambda^4 \mid Z^3 + 1)$. \\ Let $m=-1$ and proceed similarly to the first case. \end{itemize}
